title: Splitting the sky
caption: The Moon, Saturn and Mercury over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Looking west from ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, this photograph by ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek centres on the bright Moon, with ringed Saturn a little way to its upper left and rocky Mercury off to its lower left. From some latitudes, this close pairing of the two planets is tricky to pick out by eye, yet here both show clearly despite the Moon's glare.

The dusty band of the Milky Way seems to split the sky horizontally, with a star-filled night above and the last traces of sunset below. Several well-known nebulae appear along this band, including the Lagoon Nebula, the Cat's Paw Nebula and the Trifid Nebula.

Below the sky stand the individual telescopes that together make up ESO's Very Large Telescope. Its four big Unit Telescopes have mirrors 8.2 metres wide, joined by four smaller Auxiliary Telescopes whose mirrors measure 1.8 metres.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at Paranal; the source gives no camera or exposure details.
understand.eye: The camera brings out the Milky Way and its nebulae more strongly than the eye would see them, especially with the Moon so bright.

alt: The Moon with Saturn and Mercury nearby, above the band of the Milky Way and the telescopes of Paranal, with fading sunset light below.
